newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Van den Broek has tough message over Slovak vote.
newsitem.headline: Van den Broek has tough message over Slovak vote.

text.p: EU External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek visits Slovakia on Thursday with a message of concern at the failure of a weekend referendum seen as a key test of democracy.

Van den Broek arrives for a one-day visit, ahead of a final assessment next month of Slovakia's eligibility to join the European Union, but is certain to raise the failure of the referendum which was intended to ask Slovaks whether they supported NATO membership and direct presidential elections.

"At this important meeting he will make explicit the position of the EU regarding particularly the referendum, but also other events in Slovakia," EU ambassador to Slovakia Georgios Zavvos told reporters.

EU envoys expressed their concern at events surrounding the referendum, which was declared void because ballot papers were invalid, in a meeting on Wednesday with Jozef Kalman, Slovak Deputy Prime Minister in charge of EU integration.
"We were very diplomatic," one envoy told Reuters after the meeting. "Van Den Broek is coming with a really tough message."

The twinned referendums were billed as a last chance for Slovakia, which has come under fire from the West for its lack of democratic reforms, to win an invitation to join NATO in the first wave of new members.

Instead, voting was turned to chaos by a feud between Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar and President Michal Kovac, who wanted a question about presidential elections on the ballot and prompted a boycott when it was struck off at the last moment.
"In an open, straightforward and constructive way the (EU) ambassadors expressed their concerns regarding the holding of the recent referendum," Zavvos said.

Kalman said the meeting had been planned weeks in advance and only briefly touched on the referendum. "I reiterated Slovakia's declared political will to join the EU and other western and trans-Atlantic structures," he said.
The Central Referendum Committee declared the widely boycotted weekend referendum void and denounced ballot papers distributed by the Interior Ministry as a "massive swindle".
